record.paper_title: The Li–Lin’s open problem on R^N
record.context_brief: Whole-space extension of the Li–Lin problem
record.original_question: For an integer N ≥ 3, let 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2, λ > 0, and 2*(s) = 2(N − s)/(N − 2). For the whole-space Hardy–Sobolev equation −Δu + u = −λ |x|^(−s1) |u|^(p−2)u + |x|^(−s2) |u|^(q−2)u in R^N, determine whether nonzero or positive solutions exist in the critical regime 2*(s2) = q < p ≤ 2*(s1), and in the subcritical regime 2 < q < p < 2*(s1), q < 2*(s2), with q > ((2 − s2)/(2 − s1))p + (2s2 − 2s1)/(2 − s1).

evidence.quote: Motivated by resolving this open problem in more general settings, we aim to analyze how the equation’s solutions behave when the domain is an unbounded region, particularly RN. Now, we consider the Hardy-Sobolev’s critical exponents problem −∆u + u = −λ|x|−s1 |u|p−2u + |x|−s2 |u|q−2u in RN, (1.2) where N ≥ 3, λ ∈ R, 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2, 2∗(s) = 2(N − s)/(N − 2) for 0 ≤ s ≤ 2, 2 < p ≤ 2∗(s1), 2 < q ≤ 2∗(s2).
Specifically, in RN, for any λ > 0, the equation has no solution when q = 2∗(s2), while it has a solution when q < 2∗(s2).
Theorem 1.1 Suppose that 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2 and 2∗(s2) = q < p ≤ 2∗(s1). Then Problem (1.2) has no nonzero solution for all λ > 0.

Theorem 1.3 Suppose that 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2, 2 < q < p < 2∗(s1) and q < 2∗(s2). Assume that q > ((2 − s2)/(2 − s1))p + (2s2 − 2s1)/(2 − s1). Then Problem (1.2) has at least one positive solution for all λ > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N \ge 3$ be an integer. For $0 \le s \le 2$, define the Hardy–Sobolev critical exponent $2^{*}(s) = \dfrac{2(N-s)}{N-2}$. Fix parameters $0 \le s_1 < s_2 < 2$ and $\lambda > 0$, together with exponents $p,q$ satisfying $2 < p \le 2^{*}(s_1)$ and $2 < q \le 2^{*}(s_2)$. Consider the Hardy–Sobolev equation on the whole space
$$-\Delta u + u \;=\; -\lambda\, |x|^{-s_1} |u|^{p-2} u \;+\; |x|^{-s_2} |u|^{q-2} u \qquad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^N,$$
with solutions sought in the natural energy space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$.

Determine the existence of solutions in each of the following two regimes:

(a) (Critical regime) When $2^{*}(s_2) = q < p \le 2^{*}(s_1)$, decide whether (1) admits any nonzero (weak) solution for every $\lambda > 0$.

(b) (Subcritical regime) When $2 < q < p < 2^{*}(s_1)$ and $q < 2^{*}(s_2)$, with the additional constraint
$$q \;>\; \frac{2-s_2}{2-s_1}\, p \;+\; \frac{2s_2 - 2 s_1}{2-s_1},$$
decide whether (1) admits at least one positive (weak) solution for every $\lambda > 0$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem statement (whole-space extension of the Li–Lin problem) is addressed by the source itself, which establishes nonexistence of nonzero solutions in the critical regime (a) and existence of a positive solution in the subcritical regime (b) under the stated exponent condition. Hence both parts are resolved.

status_evidence.title: The Li–Lin's open problem on R^N (arXiv 2505.03613)
status_evidence.snippet: Theorem 1.1: For 2*(s2)=q<p≤2*(s1), problem has no nonzero solution for all λ>0. Theorem 1.3: Under the stated subcritical exponent inequality, problem has at least one positive solution for all λ>0.
status_evidence.claim: The two regimes asked about are answered: nonexistence in the critical case and existence of a positive solution in the subcritical case.
